requirements.evidence: Migrations match the spec: `entities_slug_unique`, cascade FKs, `owner_seq` storedAs CASE plus `entity_memberships_one_owner` (create_entity_memberships_table.php:16-27). Models, enum `manageable()`, factories with owner/admin/employee states, both policies, the `current_entity` alias (bootstrap/app.php:19), routes with `/e/switcher` declared before `{entity:slug}` (routes/web.php:27-34), /home dispatch (HomeController.php:12-28), pick with 403 and an audit log (EntityController.php:28-42), and onboarding with an overridable `uniqueSlug`, a retry on UniqueConstraintViolationException, the audit log and the session (CreateEntity.php:35-76) are all present. Switcher markup and lang keys in both locales match. Gaps: the custom `current_entity` middleware is not registered with `Livewire::addPersistentMiddleware`, and the switcher page has no `current_entity` context.

conventions.evidence: The domain write (entity + owner membership) is done inline in the Livewire component (CreateEntity.php:43-56) rather than through an `app/Actions/CreateEntity` action. Validation uses `protected function rules()` instead of the project's `#[Validate]` pattern (CreateEntity.php:27-32). `submit()` never calls `$this->authorize('create', Entity::class)` although the EntityPolicy::create ability exists. `#[Fillable]` is set deliberately on both models. Docs (docs/database-schema.md) and the CHANGELOG are updated, but the CHANGELOG entry is also copied into the already released `[0.0.0]` section (CHANGELOG.md:39).

security.evidence: Pick checks membership server-side and returns 403 before writing the session (EntityController.php:32). The middleware returns 403 for a foreign session entity and for a foreign route entity (EnsureCurrentEntity.php:30-31, 56-59). Dashboard mount authorizes `view` (Dashboard.php:17). The owner role is hard-coded server-side, so the client cannot set it (CreateEntity.php:51). Output is escaped with `{{ }}` throughout. Gaps: the Livewire `submit` action is not authorized through a policy, and `current_entity` is not a persistent Livewire middleware (security policy rule 6). Impact is limited because Dashboard has no actions and authorizes in mount.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/EntityTest.php covers DB constraints (second owner, duplicate membership, slug unique), the full policy matrices, guest/unverified redirects, /home for 0/1/>1 entities and every role, soft-deleted entities, 403 on a foreign dashboard even with a valid session, pick (audit + session) and foreign pick (session untouched), switcher markup, navbar visibility, both locales, validation, slug derivation (including trashed and reserved slugs) and the insert-time retry through a `uniqueSlug` override. Missing: an unauthorized/guest call test on the Livewire `submit` action and a tamper test, both of which the Livewire policy requires.

simplicity.evidence: Code is mostly lean. `EntityLanding` reuses the 0/1/>1 dispatch between the middleware and HomeController. There is some duplication: HomeController re-checks the session entity and then runs `Entity::findOrFail` after an `exists()` query (HomeController.php:19-20). The reserved-slug list and the MAX_ATTEMPTS loop are reasonable.

readability.evidence: Names are clear, methods are small, and the comments are useful (e.g. the owner_seq NULL comment at create_entity_memberships_table.php:17-18, the route-order comment at web.php:27). The `for ($attempt = 1; ; $attempt++)` loop with a break/catch is a bit dense but readable. The layout navbar does a `count()` query inline in Blade (default-page.blade.php:14).

scope.evidence: Nearly everything serves the task. Deleting home.blade.php follows from the new /home dispatch. The CHANGELOG entry duplicated under the released `[0.0.0]` section is an unrelated edit to release history. `EntityController::switcher` redirecting to onboarding when there are no entities is a small addition.

issues.explanation: The domain write (create entity + owner membership) lives in the Livewire component instead of an `app/Actions/CreateEntity` action that authorizes internally, as the conventions require.
The public `submit()` action never calls `$this->authorize('create', Entity::class)`, which violates Livewire security rule 3 even though the policy ability exists.
The custom `current_entity` middleware is not registered with `Livewire::addPersistentMiddleware`, so it does not apply to Livewire update requests (policy rule 6).
Uses a `rules()` method instead of the project's `#[Validate]` attribute pattern for Livewire validation.
No unauthorized-call or tamper test for the CreateEntity `submit` Livewire action, which the Livewire definition of done requires.
The new entry is also added under the already released `[0.0.0]` section, which rewrites release history.
An `exists()` query followed by `Entity::findOrFail` on the same id makes two queries where one lookup would do.
The navbar runs a membership count query on every page render from inside the Blade layout.

review.summary: The change implements the entity data model with a portable single-owner constraint, the policies, tenant session middleware, onboarding with slug retry, the switcher, the dashboard and the navbar link, and its tests are thorough and well targeted. Before merging it needs changes for project conventions and the Livewire security policy: the domain write is not in an Action, the Livewire `submit` is not authorized through the policy, validation does not use `#[Validate]`, `current_entity` is not persistent Livewire middleware, and the CHANGELOG entry is duplicated into a released section.
